verdict.rationale: Bruno stores collections, including their scripts and tests, as plain-text Bru files designed for Git. Its built-in Git UI supports init, diff, pull and commit, and the docs explicitly say you can version collections and review changes like code. Rollback is never documented as a Bruno capability; it is only implied by using Git itself. Missing for 10: documented rollback/revert of automations within Bruno, independent hands-on corroboration of the Git review workflow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Collections live as plain text files on your filesystem, so you can version them with Git and review API changes like code.
Bruno's built-in Git interface — init, diff, pull, commit, and more without leaving the app.
Core Git UI features (init, view diffs, check for updates, pull, clone) are now available in the free version.
saves API request collection files in simple, human-readable text files that are designed to be committed to a source control repo and easily shared
